newsitem.title: INDIA: India call money ends lower, security prices rally.
newsitem.headline: India call money ends lower, security prices rally.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed easy at 0.10-0.50 percent, off day's opening levels of 0.25-0.75 percent, dealers said.
Most of the deals were at 0.25 percent level, a dealer said.
"There was ample liquidity in market," she said. "Banks have already covered 100 percent ahead of reporting Friday."

The call rates in next few days will depend on the outflows from the system on account of investment in three to four day repo auctions held by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) as also 14-day treasury bills auctions, a dealer said.
"But there is also adequate liquidity in the market and the rates are unlikely to cross 5.0 percent levels," he said.
Banks were shifting from one security to another, to book profit, as there were less avenues available to depoly the excess funds, dealers said.

The 13.85 percent 2000 government stock rose to 104.95 rupees from its previous close 104.47 rupees, 11.64 percent 2000 to 99.35 rupees from 99.25 rupees, 12.14 percent 2000 to 100.50 rupees from 100.40 rupees, 12.69 percent 2002 to 100.93 rupees compared to its previous 100.90 rupees, dealers said.
A insurance company seen buying treasury bills maturing in April 1998, dealers said.
Yield on treasury bill maturing in April 1998 fell to 9.05 percent from previous 9.15 percent, dealers said.
